summary:
The statutory baseline in Austria is permissive. Same-sex relations have been legal since 1971, marriage equality has applied since 2017, and same-sex couples have held full adoption rights since 2016. The Equal Treatment Act has covered employment discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation since 2004, and recent amendments have broadened its use of "gender" to encompass gender identity, gender expression and sex characteristics; gender identity and intersex status are not named separately but are treated as covered. By January 2017 every federal state had extended anti-discrimination protection to goods and services, Lower Austria being the last to do so.

Hate speech based on sexual orientation has been prohibited since 1 January 2016, and offences committed on that ground are treated as an aggravating factor in sentencing. The 1993 Security Police Act obliges police to avoid actions that could be perceived as biased on grounds of sexual orientation.

Legal gender recognition is available without mandatory medical procedures. Following a June 2018 Constitutional Court ruling that gender identity must be accurately reflected in official documents, an "X", indeterminate or absent gender marker can be obtained; intersex people may choose "diverse", "inter" or no designation. The first non-binary passport and birth certificate were issued in 2019, but the Interior Ministry restricted the "divers" entry to holders of a medical panel certificate of intersexuality. Changing legal gender and name does not require prior sex-reassignment surgery, but the change is conditional on submitting a psychiatric opinion, and public health insurance payment for sex-change treatment is likewise bound on psychiatric opinions.

Violence risk is documented and specific. In March 2025 police uncovered a neo-Nazi network that used fake dating profiles to lure gay and bisexual men to ambushes by masked assailants, with attacks filmed and circulated. Fifteen people aged 14 to 26 were arrested over a wave of hate attacks in which at least 17 LGBTQ people were lured via fake dating-platform accounts to remote locations, ambushed, filmed and falsely accused of being paedophiles; investigators believe the true victim count is considerably higher. Official figures for 2025 record 6,751 suspected hate crimes, 7,327 prejudice motives and 1,575 victims of prejudice-related violence, with police data acknowledged to under-record; homophobic offences rose while transphobic incidents declined over the reporting year.

Detention has a specific regulatory layer. The Ludwig Boltzmann Institute's 2025 national report, produced within an EU-funded project, sets out the legal framework governing LGBTIQ people in Austrian prisons and their rights in detention, including gender self-determination and anti-discrimination protection. The Justice Ministry's answer to parliamentary question XXVIII. AB 774 of May to June 2025 states the official rules on housing transgender people in penal institutions and is the authority to cite if a trans visitor is detained; it is published in German.

Political conditions carry a documented downside. The far-right Freedom Party won the most votes in the September 2024 national election with 29.2%, its first such result since the Second World War, prompting concern about the consequences of an FPÖ-led government for LGBTQ people.

Access to care and to services is uneven in practice. Puberty blockers for young people experiencing gender dysphoria have been endorsed by the Austrian Society of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry and the Austrian Society of Gynecology and Obstetrics, and lesbian couples can access artificial insemination and IVF. In 2018 the association TeenSTAR was found to be offering minors conversion therapy classes teaching that sexual orientation was changeable; the Education Directorate Salzburg banned its workshops pending review, the association was banned in April 2019, and Parliament passed a resolution on 2 July 2019 with all parties voting in favour calling for a legal ban on conversion therapy on minors. New Ministry of Education rules restrict outside sex-education providers.

Administrative practice shows both friction and accommodation: a Vienna petition for queer sauna time slots was rejected, while Ombud guidance has been issued for gender-inclusive forms covering intersex and non-binary people. Transgender people may serve openly in the Austrian Armed Forces, a right extended since 2014, and LGBT advocacy operates openly through organisations including HOSI Wien, founded 1979, HOSI Salzburg, ALGF and Afro Rainbow Austria.
tangentialFactors:
Political visibility is high alongside the far-right advance: seven National Council politicians were openly gay after the 2019 election, Iris Eliisa Rauskala became the first openly LGBT government minister in June 2019, Georg Djundja became Austria's first openly gay mayor in April 2019, and President Alexander Van der Bellen took part in the 2019 EuroPride parade in Vienna. The ÖVP and FPÖ have historically opposed LGBT rights.

Public opinion as of 2023 showed 65% support for same-sex marriage and 66% agreeing that nothing is wrong with a same-sex relationship, while the source notes that many LGBT minorities still regard being different as a problem, a sentiment attributed to Catholic influence.

Historical prosecutions were harsh, with lesbianism criminalised after the Anschluss and 1940 court alignment to Paragraph 175; as of July 2020 no expungement or compensation scheme for historical convictions had been implemented.

Community infrastructure exists in Vienna, Linz, Innsbruck, Salzburg and Graz, with an annual Vienna Gay Pride and Regenbogenparade.

Residents changing legal gender or name must submit a psychiatric opinion, and public health insurance payment for sex-change treatment is conditional on the same documentation, which shapes domestic access to care as well as documentation.

Employment discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation has been actionable under the Equal Treatment Act since 2004, with gender identity and intersex status treated as covered under "gender"; goods and services are covered by the anti-discrimination laws of every federal state as of January 2017.

Conversion therapy for minors remains governed by a non-binding parliamentary resolution of 2 July 2019 rather than a statute, following the April 2019 prohibition of the TeenSTAR association and the Salzburg education directorate's suspension of its workshops.

Residents convicted under historical provisions have no route to expungement or compensation as of July 2020.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the 2019 parliamentary resolution calling for a statutory ban on conversion therapy on minors has since been enacted into law is unresolved in the sources reviewed; only the non-binding resolution and the TeenSTAR prohibition are documented.

The outcome of the rejected Vienna petition for queer sauna time slots, and whether any appeal followed, is not sourced.

The full text of the Justice Ministry's answer to parliamentary question XXVIII. AB 774 is in German and has not been translated here; the specific housing rules it states are therefore not reproduced.

Whether the neo-Nazi dating-profile network uncovered in March 2025 has been prosecuted to conviction, and the sentences imposed on the 15 people arrested, is unresolved in the sources reviewed.

Two reviewed sources, an Amnesty International country report and a Graz election item, yielded no substantive Austria-specific finding and are not relied on.

The 2025 hate-crime figures rest on police data that the reporting outlet acknowledges under-records, and the split between rising homophobic and declining transphobic incidents is stated without underlying counts for each category.
